title: Orientation Year Visa (Zoekjaar) Netherlands: Rules, Application & Highly Skilled Migrant Path

runs.t: The Dutch orientation year residence permit, commonly called the zoekjaar, gives eligible graduates and researchers up to one year to look for work or start a business in the Netherlands. It is not limited to graduates of Dutch universities: certain graduates of designated top-ranked institutions outside the Netherlands may also qualify. The permit provides broad work rights during that year, but it does not guarantee a job, a highly skilled migrant permit or permanent residence.

You may qualify if, within the previous three years, you completed an eligible Dutch accredited bachelor’s or master’s programme, a qualifying post-master’s programme, an eligible Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, qualifying research in the Netherlands, or a qualifying master’s/doctoral/post-master’s programme at a designated foreign institution. The permit is valid for one year and cannot be extended. The IND is the authority that decides eligibility.

rows.t: Accredited bachelor’s or master’s degree at a Dutch higher education institution, completed within three years before application.
Eligible programme lasting at least one academic year (at least 10 months), completed within the relevant three-year period.
Master’s degree obtained within the previous three years in the context of an Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programme.
Qualifying master’s, doctoral or post-master’s programme at a designated foreign educational institution; additional ranking, language and credential-evaluation conditions apply.
Qualifying scientific research conducted in the Netherlands within the previous three years under the specified residence/research conditions.

sections.title: Special rules for graduates of foreign universities

runs.t: This route can be relevant to an Indian student who graduates from a qualifying university outside the Netherlands. The institution must have been in the top 200 of the general or relevant subject rankings of at least two of the three publishers recognised by the IND: Times Higher Education, QS and ShanghaiRanking. The ranking position is assessed at the date of graduation or promotion, and subject rankings must relate to the applicant’s field.

The foreign qualification must be evaluated by Nuffic. The applicant must also satisfy one of the accepted language conditions, which can include an IELTS score of at least 6.0, an accepted equivalent test, or a qualifying English- or Dutch-taught programme. Do not assume that a university appearing in one ranking, or a high overall ranking alone, is enough.
Validity: one year. The orientation-year permit cannot be extended.
Employment: you may work for any employer without that employer obtaining a separate work permit (TWV).
Self-employment: you may work as a freelancer or start a business, subject to applicable registration, tax and other rules.
Timing: you must apply within the permitted three-year period after the qualifying graduation, research or other event.
Repeat permits: a later orientation year may be possible after a new qualifying programme or research project, subject to IND rules; it is not a simple extension.

sections.title: Applying from India or from inside the Netherlands

rows.t: Check whether an MVV is required. The IND guidance describes applying for the MVV and residence permit together through the Dutch representation, then submitting the application as instructed.
Applying from inside the Netherlands after Dutch study
Online application may be available if you hold the relevant residence permit, are registered in the BRP and have a BSN.

Use the current IND application form. Prepare passport, diploma/completion evidence, Nuffic evaluation where relevant, language evidence where required, and properly legalised/translated documents if requested.
The IND page currently lists a €254 application fee and a statutory decision period of up to 90 days. Recheck the live fee before applying.

sections.title: Moving from zoekjaar to Highly Skilled Migrant (HSM)

runs.t: To move to the highly skilled migrant route, you generally need a qualifying employment contract with an employer recognised by the IND as a sponsor, a salary meeting the applicable threshold and a salary that is in line with the market rate. The recognised employer—not the graduate acting alone—submits the HSM application.

A reduced salary criterion may apply when the HSM application is made during the orientation-year permit or within the applicable rules linked to it. The IND’s published 2026 monthly gross thresholds include €3,122 under the reduced criterion, €4,357 for migrants under 30 and €5,942 for migrants aged 30 or older. These are threshold figures, not take-home pay; check whether the salary components count and whether the relevant amount is met in the employment contract.

Important: the reduced criterion is conditional. It is not automatically available to every international graduate or for every job. Confirm the applicant’s route, timing, employer sponsorship and salary calculation directly against the IND rules in force on the application date.

sections.title: Does studying in the Netherlands lead to PR?

runs.t: No automatic PR pathway is created by graduating or holding a zoekjaar permit. A student residence permit is a temporary residence purpose. To remain long term, the graduate must qualify for an appropriate subsequent residence status and later meet the separate conditions for permanent residence or long-term EU residence. Time spent on temporary study status does not by itself guarantee that the five-year residence requirement for permanent residence will be met. Obtain individual advice before presenting a PR timeline to a student.
Identify the exact qualification, research route or programme completed.
Confirm the completion date is within the three-year application window.
For a foreign university route, check top-200 status in at least two recognised ranking publishers on the relevant date.
Confirm the subject ranking relates to the applicant’s study/research field if relying on subject rankings.
Arrange Nuffic credential evaluation for a foreign diploma.
Check accepted language evidence for the foreign-graduate route.
Check prior orientation-year permits and whether a repeat route is permitted.
Confirm MVV/application location, documents, current fee and decision timeline with IND.
If switching to HSM, verify recognised sponsor status and the applicable salary threshold.

faq.q: Can an Indian student who studied in India apply for the Dutch zoekjaar?

runs.t: Potentially, yes. The foreign-graduate route is limited to qualifying master’s, doctoral or post-master’s graduates of designated foreign institutions and has ranking, timing, language and Nuffic evaluation requirements. An Indian bachelor’s degree alone is not the route described by the IND.

faq.q: Can I work full-time during the orientation year?

runs.t: Yes. The orientation-year permit allows work without the employer obtaining a TWV, including employment and self-employment, subject to the other laws that apply.

faq.q: Is the zoekjaar automatically extended if I do not find a job?

runs.t: No. The permit is valid for one year and cannot be extended.

faq.q: Does the zoekjaar guarantee an HSM permit?

runs.t: No. You still need a recognised sponsor, a qualifying job, the required salary and compliance with IND conditions.

faq.q: Does the zoekjaar count towards permanent residence?

runs.t: Do not assume that it creates an automatic PR route. Permanent residence has separate residence-purpose and eligibility rules; seek case-specific advice.
